A blue mark is a declared value that reaches the object with no assignment in
between; an amber mark comes from a layer-2 assignment." style="text;html=0;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontFamily=Helvetica;fontSize=12;fontColor=#475569;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="40" y="1588" width="1100" height="40" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="t298" value="In-degree at least one is the in row: nothing is rendered that no declaration or assignment produced." style="text;html=0;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontFamily=Helvetica;fontSize=12;fontColor=#475569;fontStyle=1;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="40" y="1638" width="1100" height="20" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> <mxCell id="t299" value="A zero in the out column means only that this row reaches no object directly. A declared field
with no mark in either drawing is a dead declaration, and an assignment with no mark in this one
is consumed by ordering rather than serialised — the Reconcile Unit is the one such row." style="text;html=0;strokeColor=none;fillColor=none;align=left;verticalAlign=middle;fontFamily=Helvetica;fontSize=11;fontColor=#475569;" parent="1" vertex="1"> <mxGeometry x="40" y="1668" width="1100" height="60" as="geometry" /> </mxCell> </root> </mxGraphModel> </diagram> </mxfile>

g.text: The same reading. A blue mark is a declared value that reaches the object with no assignment in
between; an amber mark comes from a layer-2 assignment.
In-degree at least one is the in row: nothing is rendered that no declaration or assignment produced.
A zero in the out column means only that this row reaches no object directly. A declared field
with no mark in either drawing is a dead declaration, and an assignment with no mark in this one
is consumed by ordering rather than serialised — the Reconcile Unit is the one such row.
